title: PLA ADIZ Activity Stays Low: 2 Sorties as Han Kuang 42 Enters Final Days
detail: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense detected 2 PLA aircraft sorties, 7 PLAN vessels and 6 official ships operating around Taiwan in the 24-hour window ending 06:00 (UTC+8) on August 11, 2026, with both sorties entering Taiwan's southwestern ADIZ. Air activity held near the low end of the window's range for a second straight day, continuing the moderation seen since the August 8 spike of 14 sorties, even as Han Kuang 42 entered its final days (exercise concludes August 14) and Typhoon Dolphin approached the region.

title: US State Department Opposes China's Taiwan Strait Traffic Controls During Typhoon Dolphin
detail: The US State Department publicly opposed China's announcement that it would impose traffic-control measures on vessels transiting the Taiwan Strait ahead of Typhoon Dolphin, saying on August 11, 2026 that 'the United States opposes any actions that interfere with high seas freedoms of navigation and overflight that apply in the Taiwan Strait.' China's Guangdong Maritime Safety Administration had announced it would restrict northbound vessels entering the strait's southern approach starting 18:00 that Thursday, directing all vessels to 'comply with the measures, seek safe shelter from the storm, and follow the instructions of maritime authorities.' Taiwan's Coast Guard Administration and Mainland Affairs Council rejected the move, arguing the strait is international waters beyond Beijing's jurisdiction and accusing the CCP of asserting sovereign control 'under the pretext of a typhoon.' The dispute follows China's 'special maritime law-enforcement operations' east of Taiwan ongoing since June, which Beijing has framed as a response to Japan-Philippines maritime boundary talks.

title: Court Sentences Chinese Immigrant Xu Chunying to 7 Years for Anti-Infiltration Act Violations
detail: The New Taipei District Court sentenced Chinese immigrant Xu Chunying to seven years in prison on August 11, 2026, for violating Taiwan's Anti-Infiltration Act and Banking Act, along with fraud and helping Chinese nationals illegally enter Taiwan. Prosecutors said Xu and Cross-Strait Marriage Harmony Promotion Association chairman Chung Chin-ming maintained long-term contact with officials at China's Cross-Strait Marriage and Family Service Center and the Shanghai China Council for the Promotion of Peaceful National Reunification, accepting instructions to campaign and rally support for political candidates in Taiwan. Xu also allegedly helped two Chinese nationals enter Taiwan under the guise of a business exchange in October 2025, and separately handled roughly NT$28.75 million in underground currency exchanges and forged documents to fraudulently obtain NT$26.97 million in loans. She admitted to the fraud and currency charges but denied the infiltration-related charges and did not appear for sentencing. Xu is the ninth person — including elected officials and candidates — sentenced under the Anti-Infiltration Act since it was promulgated in 2020.
